prompt: Draft a comprehensive Product Requirements Document (PRD) for an AI-powered code review service named 'ReviewPulse'. It integrates with GitHub webhooks, scans pull requests, and provides actionable code comments.
expected_output: Produces a structured PRD containing an Executive Summary, User Personas, MoSCoW-prioritized Functional Requirements, Non-Goals, NFRs (latency, security), and executable Gherkin acceptance criteria.
assertions: Defines clear scope boundaries with explicit In-Scope Goals and Out-of-Scope Non-Goals.
Categorizes requirements into Must Have, Should Have, and Could Have tiers using MoSCoW prioritization.
Provides Given/When/Then (Gherkin) acceptance scenarios covering both successful review flows and error/edge cases.
Specifies quantifiable non-functional constraints including webhook response latency and secret sanitization.

prompt: Write an Architecture Decision Record (ADR) evaluating whether to use Apache Kafka or PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY for asynchronous event processing in our microservices platform.
expected_output: Generates a complete ADR following standard format with Title, Status, Context, Decision, Alternatives Considered (Kafka vs Postgres), Consequences (Positive, Negative, Neutral), and Compliance/Invariants.
assertions: Adheres to the standard Michael Nygard ADR format (Title, Date, Status, Deciders, Context, Decision, Consequences).
Objectively compares alternatives with concrete pros, cons, and technical trade-offs.
Explicitly articulates negative operational consequences alongside positive benefits.
Defines compliance criteria or linting invariants to enforce the architectural decision in production code.

prompt: Conduct a STRIDE threat modeling analysis for a cloud-hosted payment gateway API that receives customer credit card tokens and dispatches charge requests to payment processors.
expected_output: Generates a STRIDE threat model detailing System Boundaries, Data Flow Diagram (DFD) description, a structured threat matrix covering Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, and Elevation of Privilege, paired with mitigation controls.
assertions: Identifies system trust boundaries and external payment processor touchpoints.
Constructs a complete STRIDE matrix addressing each of the six threat categories with specific attack scenarios.
Proposes defense-in-depth mitigations (e.g. mutual TLS, tokenization, audit logging, rate limiting, and RBAC).
Classifies severity levels and defines actionable residual risk items.

prompt: Develop a test strategy and verification plan for a multi-tenant SaaS subscription billing service using the Testing Trophy methodology.
expected_output: Produces a testing matrix structured around Static Analysis, Unit, Integration, and E2E smoke tests, with explicit emphasis on integration testing against test containers, contract tests for billing webhooks, and flakiness mitigations.
assertions: Applies the Testing Trophy framework emphasizing high-confidence integration testing over shallow mocks.
Defines concrete test scenarios across data persistence, domain billing calculations, and webhook dispatching.
Outlines test double policies (fakes vs stubs vs mocks) and isolation techniques.
Includes non-functional verification including clock mocking and deterministic state reset.

prompt: We experienced a 45-minute production outage when a new database migration locked the 'orders' table during peak Black Friday traffic. Draft a blameless post-mortem report with a 5 Whys root cause analysis.
expected_output: Produces a blameless post-mortem document including Executive Summary, Impact Assessment, UTC Timeline, 5 Whys Root Cause Analysis discovering lack of expand/contract migration gates, and prioritized Prevent/Detect/Mitigate action items.
assertions: Maintains a strictly blameless tone focusing on systemic and process vulnerabilities rather than individual fault.
Constructs a chronological timeline with duration and user impact calculations.
Executes a rigorous 5 Whys analysis tracing the failure to process gaps in migration testing and rollout safety.
Formulates prioritized, actionable preventative measures with designated categories (Prevent, Detect, Mitigate).
